lead.hed: Naval Air Station Pensacola rang bells for fallen service members
lead.insight: DVIDS, posted Thursday: an Air Force airman rang a ceremonial bell at Naval Aviation Memorial Chapel during the Navy Gold Star program's Bells Across America ceremony. The photo was taken and posted Sept. 24. Remembrance, held at the same hour at chapels across the country. Not a deployment order.
lead.image_credit: U.S. Navy photo by Ens. Victoria Franklin · DVIDS 9963534 · Public domain · An Air Force airman rings a ceremonial bell at Naval Aviation Memorial Chapel, Naval Air Station Pensacola, Sept. 24, 2026.

political.hed: NATO's top U.S. commander said American support will stay critical but more limited
political.insight: Defense News, Thursday, citing Reuters: Gen. Alexus Grynkewich said the United States will keep providing critical but more limited capabilities as Europeans take a larger role. He called a limited Russian attack on NATO territory unlikely but not ruled out, and said Moscow should not try it on his watch. Interview, not a new force order.

political.hed: About one in five American students now miss 10 percent of the school year
political.insight: Heritage, Sept. 11, still the newest non-ship item in Thursday's feed: chronic absenteeism means missing about 18 days. The commentary says roughly one in five students meet that mark, about one in three in New York City public schools, and more than 40 percent in Chicago. Commentary, not a new attendance law.

political.hed: Some towns actually want growth, a forum essay argues
political.insight: Law & Liberty, Wednesday: Gary Winslett answers a forum argument that public hearings trap towns in a prisoner's dilemma, everyone wanting building somewhere else. He writes that some communities want growth. Forum essay, not a zoning vote.

tech.hed: A Navy surrogate jet flew a mission plan written for a human operator
tech.insight: Defense Daily, reprinting the Navy account: an MQ-20 Avenger surrogate tested Collaborative Autonomy Mission Planning during Gray Flag 2026 at Point Mugu, turning a human operator's plan into autonomous flight. Test report, not a fleet fielding.

tech.hed: The Army awarded Palantir $48.1 million to track ammunition
tech.insight: Defense News, Thursday: the Army gave a Palantir subsidiary a $48.1 million contract to build software that consolidates nine legacy ammunition platforms, covering the round from planning through final disposition. The service said Palantir won a three-phase selection over six weeks. Contract, not a fielded system.

culture.hed: A review asks whether Brad Pitt's wilderness film earns the survival story
culture.insight: WORLD, posted Tuesday: Heart of the Beast is rated PG-13. It follows an Army veteran stranded in the wilderness with his dog. Review, not a news dispatch. The article body sits behind the WORLD subscription wall; the title and rating are on the page.

culture.hed: Marijuana law should teach, not only shrink the black market, an essay argues
culture.insight: American Reformer, Thursday: the essay says many Christians accepted legalization as a way to shrink black markets, then argues that classical law also forms citizens. It notes a Justice Department move of FDA-approved marijuana products from Schedule I to Schedule III. Argument, not a new statute.
